senses: A little dish or vase.
ety: From Latin patella (“a small pan or dish, a plate; the kneepan, patella”), diminutive of patina (“a broad shallow dish, pan”). Doublet of paella.

senses: Of the Leguminosae family of peas, beans etc.
Resembling a legume.
ety: From Middle English leguminous, from Medieval Latin legūminōsus, ultimately from oblique stem of Latin legūmen, legūminis (“bean, pulse”) + -ous.

senses: Any agent that sensitizes something.
The degree to which something is canonical.
binge, bender, booze-up (where alcohol is drunk)
brawl, fight
ety: Bran(n)- refers to an ancient king of Wales, his name meaning "raven" in Old Welsh. His head is said to be buried under the Tower of London & is why, it is said, that ravens flock to it. "-igan" is an Anglicization of the Brythonic Gaelic surname suffix "-yggan" which means "descendant of".
examples: In the last decade of his life he went for long stretches without touching booze. Then stresses and strains would build up inside him and he would embark on a brannigan.
The second round was a brannigan from bell to bell. Both men went out for blood and both got it.

senses: A medium-sized dioecious tree, Sclerocarya birrea, indigenous to Southern Africa and West Africa.
Its edible stone fruit, with light yellow skin and white flesh.
ety: From Tswana morula (“marula tree”), or from a closely related language.
examples: They were between two marula trees.

senses: A light dumpling made of lightly spiced minced meat or fish bound with egg and poached.
An elliptical shape moulded by chefs from soft foods using two spoons.
A gesture which is usually performed by pointing one arm diagonally downwards palm down, while touching the shoulder with the opposite hand, in a manner similar to an inverted Nazi salute.
ety: Borrowed from French quenelle, from German Knödel. Doublet of knaidel.

senses: The flowering plant Orontium aquaticum.
ety: From Powhatan tockawhoughe. The "person" sense implies that such a person was so poor as to be reduced to eating the root.

senses: Wavy; curly, as hair.
ety: From the verb to buckle, equivalent to buckle + -ing.

senses: Of or referring to gelatin.
ety: From gelatine + -ous; probably modeled on French gélatineux.

senses: The removal of chlorine from water that has been chlorinated
Of the metacarpus.
A visual representation of a dog made from snow.
examples: Jeremy Fisher, 13, spent a good part of the afternoon building four snowmen and a snowdog outside his home on Main Street in the Broad Brook section of East Windsor.
They then build a giant snowdog together and the ending builds up gradually as the snowdog slowly melts over the weeks.
Reagan quickly put the snow to good use, making a snowman in 45 minutes and even a snowdog complete with leash and sunglasses.

senses: Administered as a gas or vapour that is inhaled
A device which suppresses something, especially an electronic or mechanical device.
A device added to the barrel of a firearm which reduces the noise and flash generated by firing the weapon.
A person who suppresses others, a tyrant.
Of, or like, cord; having cords or cord-like parts.
The act or process of skeletonizing.
A stranger; anybody; any old person.
examples: Is that an open invitation to all and sundry randomers?

senses: That can be scanned; suitable for scanning.
A resinous exudation from various tropical trees, especially Hymenaea courbaril and Schinus terebinthifolia, used chiefly in making varnishes and printing ink.
ety: From Spanish copal, from Classical Nahuatl copalli (“incense”).

senses: a machine that produces cold air, either for air conditioning, to prepare chilled foods etc.
a heat exchanger between a coolant and a refrigerant, to transfer heat from the coolant loop into the refrigeration system
A machine that removes heat from the working fluid in a refrigeration cycle
A frightening dramatic work, such as a book or film
A person who has a schizoaffective disorder.
A chant or anthem recited after a reading in a church service; a respond.
A book of liturgical responses; a responsorial.
ety: Inherited from Middle English responsorie, from Late Latin respōnsōrium, from Latin respōnsus (“answered”), from the verb respondeō (“to answer”). Compare respond.

senses: Any of several stringed instruments of Latino origin; a Venezuelan ukulele-like instrument with four strings; a Puerto Rican violin-like instrument with ten strings in five courses (most commonly).
ety: From Spanish cuatro. Doublet of four and quatre.

senses: Japanese maple (Acer palmatum)
A bank holding company.
examples: While we have seen some group banks fail, several of the present bancorporations have shown statements that indicate a high degree of liquidity.

senses: A person who chops wood; a lumberjack
A person who woodchops as a sport
An administrative district in parts of South Asia.
ety: From Bengali মৌজা (mōuja) and Urdu موضع (mauze', mauza'). Doublet of moza.

senses: A sort of trim added to the neckline of a dress.
Difficult to understand; complicated.
examples: These vulgar, pleasure-seeking people, so frank and clamorous, were too uninhibited for his shielded and involuted life.

senses: Vermilion; bright red.
Silver gilt or gilt bronze.
A liquid composition applied to a gilded surface to give luster to the gold.
ety: From Middle English vermayle, from Old French vermeil (“vermilion”), from Latin vermiculus (“little worm”), from vermis (“worm”), ultimately in reference to Kermes vermilio, a type of scale insect used to make a crimson dye. Doublet of vermicule.

senses: Somewhat large.
examples: Humans, buffered by cultural and behavioral options, can often tolerate largish changes in climatic conditions.

senses: Power or strength; potency.
A stud that acts as a support of a pivot in a watch or clock.
ety: Borrowed from Middle French potence (“power, a crutch”), from Latin potentia (“power, in Medieval Latin also crutch”), from potens (“powerful”); see potent.

senses: An oval gold coin in the Edo period of feudal Japan.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 小判(こばん) (koban).
examples: It contained, as usual, nothing but an invitation to come to Edo to confer on matters respecting which it did not enter into any particulars, with an offer of three koban for the expenses of the journey.

senses: Often preceded by the: amusement, fun, especially through enjoyable company; also, pleasant conversation.
ety: Variant of crack, respelled after Irish craic (itself a borrowing from English).

senses: A small pennant or banner carried by infantry soldiers to direct troop movement.
A soldier assigned to carry such a banner.
ety: From French guidon, from Italian guidone. Equivalent of guide + on.

senses: A male bomber (person who sets bombs)
A strain of bacteria that is resistant to many antibiotics (e.g., MDR, XDR).
Any pathogen resistant to many, even all, of the biocides or other agents used to treat similar pathogens.
An invasive insect, Bemisia tabaci, that is a major pest of vegetable crops, both directly and as a virus vector.
A person who responds to an emergency situation or other summons.
Military equipment, apparatus, and supplies.
ety: Borrowed from French matériel. Doublet of material.
